summary: New box Preterit-wa: example for sense 1 in Preterit-wa (MAC NE Interview 2/214)

data.translation: So, during the Firman those ones had scattered as well ...

rationale: New Preterit-wa box; anterior dispersal, source ending retained.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (JTM 5.2/82)

data.turoyo: i naqqa d məlla Zin ha Zin, hani tayihi. tayihi komər l aḏiʕi ayko əzzən.
data.translation: Als sie sagte: Zīn, auf geht’s Zīn, gerieten sie in Verwirrung. Sie gerieten in Verwirrung und wussten nicht mehr, wohin sie gehen sollten.

rationale: Thin Preterit Intransitive cell; repeated wandering/disorientation with explicit inability to find a direction.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (MAC NE Interview 2/213)

data.translation: They went away, they fled at the time of the Firman!

rationale: Thin cell; completed dispersal during the Firman, with source English retained.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (111/23)

data.turoyo: Komər Hetim azze, tayəh, azzele l balad raḥuqo.
data.translation: Hatim streifte nun in der weltumher und ging in ein fernes Land.

rationale: Thin Preterit Intransitive cell; singular base tayəh with destination.

summary: Plural dispersal and singular wandering remain within inherited I.1. Human groups fleeing and cats wandering are participant changes, not separate senses.
Completed tayihi contrasts with anterior tayihiwa and indicative Ktayhi. The new Preterit-wa box is distinct from Infectum-wa; no new base form is reconstructed.
The adjacent MAC Interview /213–215 clauses are repeated descriptions of the same dispersal; /213 is selected, /215 adds no independent example.
The mountain clause in PrS 57/7 matches the inherited prs 152/29 quotation. Its reference-system difference is retained as a question.
JTM 5.2/82: do the men physically scatter aimlessly or first become mentally confused? The present evidence does not warrant a separate purely mental sense.
Reconcile PrS 57/7 with inherited prs 152/29 before changing the citation.
Panic can accompany losing one’s bearings; the directional sequel does not decide between actual scattering and an initial mental state. No separate mental meaning is published.
